## Problem
When using NVM (Node Version Manager), the standard installation and usage instructions for MCP servers don't work. The app tries to use an incorrect Node and fails.

## Workaround

1. Avoid `npx`, install packages globally.
2. Use absolute paths to both the Node executable and server script.

Example:

{

items.title: MCP Servers Don't Work with NVM

items.author: minduch
items.body:
## Summary

`@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` v0.2.0 (`secure-filesystem-server`) crashes
on startup if **any** allowed directory in `argv` does not exist. The crash is caused
by `Promise.all(dirs.map(fs.stat))` rejecting on the first ENOENT, which terminates
the entire startup with no fallback and no actionable stderr captured by hosts that
don't surface child-process stderr (e.g. Claude Desktop on Windows MSIX, see linked
report).

## Reproduction

```bash
node dist/index.js "C:\exists" "C:\does-not-exist"
```

Output:
Error accessing directory C:\does-not-exist: Error: ENOENT: no su
items.title: [server-filesystem] Single missing allowed-directory causes silent process exit due to Promise.all rejection
